City Council Meeting
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
City Council, Community Development Financing Authority, Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*
June 18, 2012
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Ury at 05:02 p.m. , on June 18, 2012, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.
A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by 5:00 p.m. on June 15, 2012, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.
*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."
Present:
Council Member Kelley
Council Member Leckness
Council Member Schlicht
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon
Mayor Ury
Absent:
None
Staff Present:
Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager
William P Curley III, City Attorney
Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
Karen Hamman, City Clerk
PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Schlicht
INVOCATION: Council Member Kelley
CLOSED SESSION
CS1.
Conference With Legal Counsel - Anticipated Litigation: Initiation of Litigation pursuant to Subdivision (c) of section 54956.9 (one case.)
CS2.
Labor Negotiations - The City Council will Provide Direction to its Labor Negotiator Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.6. The Parties to the Negotiations are the City and the City's Unrepresented Employees. The City's Negotiator is Dennis Wilberg.
RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE
At the hour of 5:06 p.m., Mayor Pro Tem Reardon recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council reconvened at 6:09 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.
REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION
City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the City Council dealt with Closed Session Item CS1. The Council did not authorize commencement of litigation at this time but staff will monitor the situation. Mr. Curley noted that item CS2 was not addressed and will be considered at a future meeting.
PRESENTATIONS
P1.
Recognize City Volunteers, for Their 1,000 Hours of Service
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon presented certificates of appreciation to (1) Elizabeth Busick for volunteer hours with the Mission Viejo Library, (2) Bill McArtney for volunteer hours with the Senior Community Activity Team (SCAT), and (3) Kay Palmieri and Neysa Soafer for volunteer hours with the Norman P. Community & Senior Center.
P2.
Presentation by the Dedicated Animal Welfare Group Regarding the Annual Mission Viejo DAWG WALK
Sharon Cody announced that the 2012 DAWG Walk will be held on Saturday, June 23 and she invited the community to attend.
P3.
Recognition of Raul Villalobos for his Dedication and Hard Work in Support of the South Mission Viejo Little League
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon presented a certificate of appreciation to City employee Raul Villalobos.
P4.
Presentation by the South Orange County Regional Chamber of Commerce
The City Council received a presentation from Jim Leach, Chief Executive Officer of the South Orange County Economic Coalition, a division of the South Orange County Regional Chamber of Commerce, entitled “Speaking Up For the Regional Business Community."
PUBLIC COMMENTS
Larry Gilbert, M.V.: discussed the Kaleidoscope signage proposal and he quoted Lake Forest Mayor Kathryn McCullough who is opposed to electronic billboard signage. He also read from a letter of opposition submitted by the City of Laguna Hills. Mr. Gilbert concluded his comments by urging residents to opt out of the Edison Smart Meter installation. Michael Valdez, M.V.: expressed concern with a recent decision of the Planning and Transportation Commission to allow a 7-11 convenience store at the corner of Marguerite Parkway and Trabuco.
Wendy Bucknum, M.V.: announced that she recently toured the Marguerite Tennis Center and recreation complex. She stated that there has been an amazing transformation and she encouraged residents to visit the new facility. Mrs. Bucknum outlined her attendance at a Flag Day ceremony at Fairhaven Memorial and she thanked the City Council for supporting grad night activities for all of the high schools in Mission Viejo. Lastly, she discussed her attendance at the “Overtaken” film preview and she pledged her support to help make sure that all middle school children see the film.
CONSENT CALENDAR
Items 12 and 14 were removed from the Consent Calendar for discussion. Mayor Ury allowed staff to answer a question on item 15 but it was not removed from the Calendar for separate consideration.
Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, seconded by Mayor Ury, to approve the Consent Calendar as described below.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
1.
Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions
Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further reading waived.
2.
City Council Minutes
Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of June 4, 2012, as presented.
3.
General Municipal Election - November 6, 2012
(1) Adopted Resolution 12-32 Calling for the Holding of a General Municipal Election to be Held on Tuesday, November 6, 2012, for the Election of Certain Officers as Required by the provisions of the laws of the State of California Relating to General Law; (2) adopted Resolution 12-33 Requesting the Board of Supervisors of the County of Orange to Consolidate a General Municipal Election to be Held on November 6, 2012, with the Statewide General Election to be Held on the Same Date Pursuant to §10403 of the Elections Code; (3) adopted Resolution 12-34 Adopting Regulations for Candidates for Elective Office Pertaining to Candidates Statements Submitted to the Voters at an Election to be Held on Tuesday, November 6, 2012; and (4) directed the City Clerk to schedule the adoption of the resolution citing the election results and the administration of the oath to the newly elected Council Members on December 3, 2012, or as soon as possible thereafter.
4.
Infrastructure Safe Route to School Sidewalk and Ramp Improvements-Napoli Way Sidewalk Gap Closure and Various Curb Ramp Improvements (CIP 211)
Approved the bid specifications and authorized staff to advertise for construction bids for the subject project.
5.
Check Register Dated May 25, 2012 in the Amount of $577,040.60
Ratified the accompanying check register.
6.
Check Register Dated June 1, 2012 in the Amount of $1,043,197.31
Ratified the accompanying check register.
7.
Establishment of the Child Abuse and Neglect Reporting Procedure Personnel Policy
Adopted Resolution 12-35 Providing for the Establishment of a Child Abuse and Neglect Reporting Procedure Personnel Policy.
8.
City Treasurer's Monthly Report for April 2012
Received and filed.
9.
Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA) Treasurer's Monthly Report for April 2012
Received and filed.
10.
Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer's Monthly Report for April 2012
Received and filed.
11.
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer's Monthly Report for April 2012
Received and filed.
13.
State-Local Partnership Program Formula Grant for Jeronimo Road Resurfacing Project (CIP837)
Adopted Resolution 12-37 Authorizing Application for Funds for the State-Local Partnership Program Under the Proposition 1B Highway Safety, Traffic Reduction, Air Quality, and Port Security Bond Act of 2006 for Jeronimo Road Resurfacing, Los Alisos Boulevard to Marguerite Parkway Project.
15.
FY 2012-13 Law Enforcement Services Agreement and Additional Special Enforcement Services Provided by the Orange County Sheriff’s Department
Emergency Services Manager Paul Catsimanes presented the staff report and explained special enforcement services and the reimbursement that is provided for these services under separate billing.
(1) Approved the FY 2012-13 Law Enforcement Services Agreement with the County of Orange (A12-18) for an amount not to exceed $15,471,819; and (2) authorized the City Manager to approve reimbursements related to special enforcement services in an amount not to exceed $65,000 for FY 2012-13.
16.
Destruction of Records - Citywide 2011 Records Purge
Adopted Resolution 12-38 Authorizing and Directing the City Clerk to Destroy Certain City Records and Documents Pursuant to the Government Code of the State of California.
17.
Mission Viejo Community Facilities District No 92-1 - Annual Special Tax for Fiscal Year 2012-13
Adopt Resolution 12-39 Establishing an Annual Special Tax for Fiscal Year 2012-13 for Community Facilities District No. 92-1 (Mission Viejo Freeway Center.)
18.
Provide Technology Services to Cities of Laguna Niguel and Laguna Woods
Authorized staff to respond to Requests for Proposals from the Cities of Laguna Niguel and Laguna Woods.
ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR
12.
Unappropriate General Fund Reserves from the Oso Parkway Widening, I-5 to Country Club Drive CIP Project (791)
City Manager Wilberg presented the staff report.
Motion made by Mayor Ury, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to adopt Resolution 12-36 Amending the Fiscal Year 2011-2012 Budget for Costs Related to Capital Improvement Project 791.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, Mayor Ury, Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, and Council Member Kelley
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
14.
Legislative Advocacy and Government Relations Services
City Manager Wilberg presented the staff report.
Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, seconded by Mayor Ury, to approve the proposed Professional Services Agreement with Townsend Public Affairs (A12-17) for state legislative advocacy and government relations services for a total not to exceed amount of $60,000 for the period of July 1, 2012, to June 30, 2013.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
Council Member Schlicht
ABSENT:
None
PUBLIC HEARINGS
NEW BUSINESS
20.
Proposed Reduction of the Cat Adoption Fee for the Animal Services Program
The following presented written comments in support of the proposed reduction in cat adoption fees: Sharon Cody, M.V.; Teresa Mahlberg, Lake Forest; Jane Lucas, Rancho Santa Margarita; and Erin Flair, Laguna Niguel.
Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, to adopt Resolution 12-40 Amending the Fines and Fees of the Mission Viejo Animal Services Program.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
21.
Legal Services for Oversight Board
City Manager Wilberg presented the staff report.
Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Leckness, to issue an RFP on behalf of the Oversight Board with funding coming from the administrative budget of the Successor Agency.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
OLD BUSINESS
19.
Discussion of Alternatives to Adopting Proposed Ordinance Designating Very High Fire Hazard Severity Zones within the City of Mission Viejo
Mayor Ury announced that he and Council Member Leckness would recuse themselves from the discussion due to a potential conflict of interest because of the proximity of their homes to the proposed Very High Fire Hazard Severity Zone. Mr. Ury and Mr. Leckness left the room at 7:09 p.m. and Mayor Pro Tem Reardon assumed the role of chair of the meeting.
Community Development Director Chuck Wilson presented the staff report.
Mayor Ury and Council Member Leckness returned to the room at 7:48 p.m.
Laura Blaul, Orange County Fire Authority, Irvine: discussed recommendations 3 and 4 as outlined in the staff report and she stated that OCFA recommends that the Council approve option 3.
Sivon Kalminov, M.V.: thanked the City Council for doing the right thing for residents of the community. He also asked why residents who are potentially impacted by the fire zones were not notified that the Council would be considering this matter as they had been notified of a prior consideration in March.
Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: stated that the Council directed the Fire Authority to complete six action items in March and he inquired as to the status of those items. He further asked OCFA representatives if they have completed all six items.
Steve Dibble, President of the Cordova Homeowners Association, M.V.: expressed support for alternative 4 or option 3 if the fire maps are removed.
The following presented written comments in favor of option 4: Derik and Kristen Van Leewen, M.V.; Herbert Hoeschele, M.V.; Gregory Woodard, M.V.; Tracy Dean, M.V.; and Doreen McKernan, M.V.
Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, to free form to remove from consideration recommendations 1 and 2.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, Council Member Schlicht, and Council Member Kelley
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
RECUSE:
Mayor Ury, and Council Member Leckness.
Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Leckness, to approve alternative 3 to reject the Very High Fire Hazard Severity Zone Map with appropriate findings and designate a Special Fire Protection Area within the City.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
Council Member Schlicht
ABSENT:
None
Council Member Schlicht stated for the record that she voted no because she believes that the 15,000 affected property owners should have been notified of the agenda item prior to the Council Meeting.
MAYOR'S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS
22.
Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report
Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: announced that OCFA is the subject of an ongoing investigation by the Orange County Grand Jury. He encouraged anyone with information or concern to contact the Grand Jury.
Council Member Kelley presented the report.
23.
Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report
Mayor Ury presented the report.
24.
San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon presented the report.
25.
SCAG Transportation & Communications Committee (TCC) Report
Council Member Kelley presented the report.
26.
CUSD Ad Hoc Committee
Council Member Kelley presented the report.
STAFF REPORTS
City Manager’s Report
City Manager Wilberg drew the Council’s attention to agenda item 18 and commended Information Technology Director Jackie Alexander for reaching the point and capability of providing IT service to neighboring cities. Ms. Alexander has completed a proposal for Laguna Woods and she will be working on a proposal for the City of Laguna Niguel over the coming week.
City Attorney’s Report
27.
Ordinance Repealing the Requirement that City Contractors Use the E-Verify Program
City Attorney Bill Curley presented the staff report and recommended the Council address item 29 before making a decision on this matter.
Matt Corrigan, M.V.: encouraged the Council Members to approve the E-Verify proposal in item 29.
Motion made by , seconded by , to
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon
29.
E-Verify
Resident Steve Serra outlined the proposal to make inoperative and suspend enforcement of the City contractor E-Verify requirement.
The following presented written comments in favor of the proposal: Dale Tyler, M.V.; Matt Trudell, M.V.; Matt Corrigan, M.V.; M.B. McDougall, M.V.; Brian Wetmore, M.V.; Margo Kutner, M.V.; and John Paul Ledesma, M.V.
City Attorney Curley announced that the Council could adopt a similar product by way of a Resolution, rather than an Ordinance.
No action was taken at this time.
COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS (Continued)
28.
Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended
The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.
Council Member Kelley
Council Member Kelley announced that the CUSD budget adoption is scheduled for June 27, 2012, and she encouraged residents who have any input to contact the Board Trustees and to follow the proposed budget. Council Member Kelley congratulated and thanked the volunteers who were recognized at the beginning of the meeting and she announced that the City Council will soon receive an update on the Healthy Eating Active Living (HEAL) initiative which was adopted a year ago. She noted that there will be a Community Health Fair in conjunction with the Farmers Market on July 13 and she will provide additional details at the next Council Meeting. Council Member Kelley announced that she is sorry she will miss the DAWG Walk and Pet Faire on June 23 but she encouraged residents to attend this wonderful annual event. She also outlined her attendance at recent events including a proposed Sober High School presentation on June 6 and the Community of Character Youth Committee Gala on June 9.
Council Member Leckness
Council Member Leckness outlined his attendance at the Carl Hankey California Distinguished School presentation where he enjoyed learning about the school’s namesake. He also discussed his attendance at the Casta Del Sol Republican luncheon where Michael Reagan, son of President Reagan, was the keynote speaker. Mr. Reagan shared an interesting story about his sister, Maureen, recommending to her father that he appoint a woman to the Supreme Court. Not long afterward President Regan appointed Sandra Day O’Connor, the first United States Supreme Court Justice.
Council Member Schlicht
Council Member Schlicht stated that she is disappointed with her Council colleague’s action regarding the fire maps. She doesn’t think there is an understanding that they have now created a special fire protection area for half of the City. She noted that homebuyers will purchase property outside of the fire protection area and she doesn’t think her colleagues are aware of the ramifications of their vote. She stated that there will be some negative impacts on the 15,000 residents of the fire protection area and those homeowners had a right to be at the Council meeting and should have been notified. Council Member Schlicht reminded residents that they have an opportunity to opt out of the Edison Smart Meters. She stated that citizen activism is very important to the City and to the nation and a local activist, Wayne Tait, is the spokesperson for a new group called Hold CUSD Accountable. She suggested that parents of CUSD students contact Mr. Tait at (949) 246-7688 and get involved. Council Member Schlicht also announced that the Saddleback Republican Assembly will host CUSD Trustee Addonizio on Thursday June 21, 2012, at 7:00 p.m. the Murray Center and Ms. Addonizio will inform residents of what is happening at CUSD. Additionally, on June 21, the Mission Viejo Chamber of Commerce will hold its monthly mixer at the YMCA from 5:30 to 7:30 p.m. Council Member Schlicht concluded her comments with a quote from a Mission Viejo resident, Mr. Kiss: "Be brave enough to stand up for what is right, although it may not be popular or easy, and even if you stand alone."
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon announced that she will return at the Council Meeting of July 2 with a draft resolution similar to the proposed E-Verify ordinance that was presented for item 29. She will work with resident Steve Serra and the City Attorney to make the necessary adjustments in the language. Mayor Pro Tem Reardon thanked Assistant City Manager Rattay and Council Member Kelley for their work with the Overtaken movie event at Kaleidoscope. She stated that the issue of prescription drug overdose is a matter of public health and safety and she pledged her support to make Mission Viejo students aware of the problem and to give them the opportunity to see the movie Overtaken. She announced that she attended the retirement celebration for Sergeant Major Anthony Sammartino and it was one of the most wonderful experiences she has had. She noted that it was very clear that he is loved by the people he has led in the Marines. Mayor Pro Tem Reardon thanked Council Member Kelley for getting the City started with the Marine Adoption Committee and she thanked the committee members for organizing events and going above and beyond to provide support for the Marines. Lastly, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon announced that she attended the Community of Character annual event and she is extremely impressed by the skill sets of these young people.
Mayor Ury
Mayor Ury discussed the fire map issue and reminded his colleagues that the Council’s goal has been to find a way around adoption of the state maps and he complimented his colleagues for the work that was done to come up with alternatives. Mayor Ury stated that he is continually amazed that every time the Council puts a lot of good work and effort in to something, there are those who make it their job to professionally criticize everything that goes on. He reminded his colleagues that the fire map matter will come back at another meeting and although everyone is not going to be pleased at all times, he finds it interesting that some people are not pleased all of the time. Mayor Ury announced that he recently visited the San Onofre Nuclear station and he has a stronger understanding of some of the challenges that are going on there. He also attended a ceremony at Reilly Elementary to commemorate Flag Day and to celebrate the retirement of Principal Judy Shades. He noted that the character program is in full bloom at the school and he was very impressed.
30.
Status Update on the City’s "Improve Don’t Move" Fee Waiver and Reduction Program for Residential and Commercial Building Permits
Community Development Director Chuck Wilson presented an update on the Improve Don’t Move Program and announced that the City has waived approximately $318,312 in residential building permit fees and $54,698 in commercial building permit fees. The total valuation of economic development as a result of this program is just over $20 million.
ADJOURNMENT
At the hour of 10:06 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session, Mayor Ury adjourned the meeting to Monday, July 2, 2012, at 5:00 p.m.
______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk
Approved at the meeting of July 02, 2012
